extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and supervisory patent examiners (also patent applicants and their attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for examiners on preparing Office actions and related communications, including how to search and cite prior art, what to include in rejections/allowances, copy-provision policies, and supervisory review expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough examination and prior art investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: On taking up an application for examination ... the examiner shall make a thorough study thereof and shall make a thorough investigation of the available prior art relating to the subject matter of the claimed invention. The examination shall be complete with respect both to compliance of the application or patent under reexamination with the applicable statutes and rules and to the patentability of the invention as claimed, as well as with respect to matters of form, unless otherwise indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must fully study the application and search relevant prior art; completeness covers statutory/rule compliance, patentability, and form matters. See exceptions where action may be limited (e.g., misjoinder, fundamental defects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of examiner's action and reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant ... will be notified of the examiner’s action. The reasons for any adverse action or any objection or requirement will be stated in an Office action and such information or references will be given as may be useful in aiding the applicant ... to judge the propriety of continuing the prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office actions must state reasons for rejections/objections and include useful information/references to help applicants evaluate whether to continue prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: International-type search availability
rubrics_metrics.description: An international-type search will be made in all national applications filed on and after June 1, 1978. Any national application may also have an international-type search report prepared thereon at the time of the national examination on the merits, upon specific written request therefor and payment of the international-type search report fee set forth in § 1.21(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement describing when international-type searches are performed and how to request one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness may be limited in certain circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s action will be complete as to all matters, except that in appropriate circumstances, such as misjoinder of invention, fundamental defects in the application, and the like, the action of the examiner may be limited to such matters before further action is made. However, matters of form need not be raised by the examiner until a claim is found allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fundamental problems exist, examiner can limit scope of action; form objections can be deferred until allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejections must cite best references and explain pertinence
rubrics_metrics.description: In rejecting claims for want of novelty or for obviousness, the examiner must cite the best references at his or her command. When a reference is complex or shows or describes inventions other than that claimed by the applicant, the particular part relied on must be designated as nearly as practicable. The pertinence of each reference, if not apparent, must be clearly explained and each rejected claim specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite the best prior art; identify the exact parts relied upon; explain why each reference is pertinent; specify which claims are rejected. For 35 U.S.C. 103 rejections, set out how references are modified or combined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible reliance on admissions and personal-knowledge facts
rubrics_metrics.description: In rejecting claims the examiner may rely upon admissions by the applicant ... and, insofar as rejections in applications are concerned, may also rely upon facts within his or her knowledge pursuant to paragraph (d)(2) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners can use applicant admissions and personal-knowledge facts; when relying on facts within personal knowledge, the data shall be as specific as possible and must be supported, when called for by the applicant, by the affidavit of such employee (subject to contradiction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of subject matter as commonly owned (102/103/c and joint research agreements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter which would otherwise qualify as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) ... will be treated as commonly owned for purposes of 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) if the applicant or patent owner provides a statement ... Subject matter ... will be treated as commonly owned ... on the basis of a joint research agreement under 35 U.S.C. 102(c) if: (A) The applicant or patent owner provides a statement ... and (B) The application ... discloses or is amended to disclose the names of the parties to the joint research agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid certain prior-art effects based on common ownership or joint research, applicants/patent owners must provide specific statements and, for JRAs, disclose parties' names; similar provisions apply under pre- and post-2013 statutory schemes (see subsections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required bibliographic data when citing references
rubrics_metrics.description: If domestic patents are cited by the examiner, their numbers and dates, and the names of the patentees will be stated. If domestic patent application publications are cited ... their publication number, publication date, and the names of the applicants will be stated. If foreign published applications or patents are cited, their nationality or country, numbers and dates, and the names of the patentees will be stated ... If printed publications are cited, the author (if any), title, date, pages or plates, and place of publication, or place where a copy can be found, will be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient bibliographic detail so applicant (or patent owner) can identify and obtain cited documents; when only part of a foreign doc is involved, identify particular pages/sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for allowance must be stated when unclear
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner believes that the record of the prosecution as a whole does not make clear his or her reasons for allowing a claim or claims, the examiner may set forth such reasoning. The reasons shall be incorporated into an Office action rejecting other claims ... or be the subject of a separate communication to the applicant or patent owner. The applicant or patent owner may file a statement commenting on the reasons for allowance within such time as may be specified by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit reasons for allowance where the record is unclear; allow applicant/patent owner opportunity to comment; failure to respond does not imply consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of Office action and attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office action may include objections to the disclosure, an explanation of references cited but not applied, an indication of allowable subject matter, other requirements (including requirements for restriction if applicable), and other pertinent comments. The list of references cited appears on a separate form, Notice of References Cited, PTO-892 ... The attachments have the same paper number and are to be considered as part of the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office actions should include appropriate objections, explanations, indications of allowable subject matter, restriction requirements, and attach PTO-892 and other relevant documents as part of the action; avoid including matters unrelated to examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Office Action Summary Form PTOL-326 for first actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the current first action procedure, the examiner signifies on the Office Action Summary Form PTOL-326 certain information including the period set for reply, any attachments, and a 'Summary of Action,' which is the position taken on all the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTOL-326 is to be used with all first Office actions to summarize reply period, attachments, and claim positions; PTOL-90 may be used as a coversheet for correspondence address and mail date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide information useful in judging propriety of continuing prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Information useful in judging the propriety of continuing the prosecution may include, for example, the identification and a brief discussion of the particular figure(s) of the drawing(s), and/or page(s) or paragraph(s) of the best reference(s) cited by the examiner, the applicant, or a foreign office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When citing prior art, point applicants to specific figures/pages/paragraphs and briefly discuss relevance to help them decide whether to continue prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may indicate interviews could result in agreements; interview practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner, in the exercise of their professional judgment, is permitted to indicate that an interview with applicant’s representative may result [in agreements whereby the application may be placed in condition for allowance]. Any amendment agreed upon during an interview may be made either by the applicant’s attorney or agent or by the examiner in an examiner’s amendment. It should be recognized that when extensive amendments are necessary it would be preferable if they were filed by the attorney or agent of record ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage interviews where helpful; use AIR Form to schedule; prefer attorney/agent to file extensive amendments to preserve file wrapper record; see MPEP § 713 for interview practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include identifying information in replies and filings to expedite handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies to Office actions should include the application number as well as the 4-digit art unit number and the examiner’s name to expedite handling within the Office. Further, applicants are encouraged to include the 4-digit confirmation number on every paper filed in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include application number, art unit, examiner name, and confirmation number to speed processing; see MPEP § 503 for confirmation number explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs for examiner contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 7.100 Name And Number of Examiner To Be Contacted ... Any inquiry concerning this communication should be directed to [1] at telephone number [2]. ... ¶ 7.101 Telephone Inquiry Contacts- Non 5/4/9 Schedule ... insert name, telephone number, days and hours, supervisor contact info, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use designated form paragraphs and fill all bracketed items (examiner name, phone, duty hours, SPE name/phone) so applicants know whom to contact and when; include supervisor contact if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary examiner responsibilities when mentoring assistants
rubrics_metrics.description: After the search has been completed, action is taken in the light of the references found. Where the assistant examiner has been in the Office but a short time, it is the duty of the primary examiner to review the application thoroughly. The primary examiner may indicate the action to be taken, whether restriction or election of species is to be required, or whether the claims are to be considered on their merits. If action on the merits is to be given and claims rejected, the primary examiner may indicate how the references are to be applied ... The primary examiner may authorize allowance if all statutory requirements are met and no further field of search is known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary examiners must review junior examiners' work, guide on restriction/election, application of references, and authorize allowance only when statutory requirements are satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervisory review for third-action and long-pending applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The supervisory patent examiners should impress upon their assistants that the shortest path to the final disposition of an application is by finding the best references on the first search and carefully applying them. The supervisory patent examiners are expected to personally check on the pendency of every application which is up for the third or subsequent Office action with a view to finally concluding its prosecution. Any application that has been pending five years or more should be carefully studied ... and every effort should be made to terminate its prosecution. In order to accomplish this result, the application is to be considered 'special' by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supervisors must monitor third+ action and 5-year applications to conclude prosecution and consider such applications special to focus termination efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners should cite prior art nearest to the claimed subject matter and explain relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: During the examination ... the examiner should cite appropriate prior art which is nearest to the subject matter defined in the claims. When such prior art is cited, its pertinence should be explained. The examiner must consider all the prior art references (alone and in combination) cited in the application or reexamination, including those cited by the applicant in a properly submitted Information Disclosure Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite the closest prior art, explain pertinence, and consider all references on the record including IDS submissions; form paragraph 7.96 may be used as an introductory sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy for furnishing copies of cited references to applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of cited foreign patent documents and non-patent literature references (except as noted below) are automatically furnished without charge to applicant together with the Office action in which they are cited. Copies of the cited references are also placed in the application file for use by the examiner during the prosecution. Copies of U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications are not provided in paper to applicants and are not placed in the application file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign patents and NPL are furnished automatically (with exceptions); U.S. patents and publications are not provided in paper. Examiner should mark PTO-892 appropriately and include references in the action folder; missing references will cause return of the application until obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: When references are not furnished to applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of references cited by applicant in accordance with MPEP §§ 609, 707.05(b) and 708.02 are not furnished to applicant with the Office action. Additionally, copies of references cited in the parent application are not furnished in continuation applications if they had been previously cited in the parent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant-submitted citations and parent-app references already in file need not be re-furnished; examiner should check the left hand column of PTO-892 to know whether not to furnish a copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: References cited at time of allowance must be furnished and listed for printing
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of foreign patent documents and nonpatent literature which are cited by the examiner at the time of allowance will be furnished to applicant with the Office action and be retained in the file wrapper. Allowed applications should generally contain a citation of pertinent prior art for printing in the patent, even if no claim presented during the prosecution was considered unpatentable over such prior art. Only in those instances where a proper search has not revealed any prior art relevant to the claimed invention is it appropriate to send an application to issue with no art cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure pertinent prior art is listed for printing in the patent; if none, indicate 'None' on PTO-892. In continuing applications, list parent's cited references on PTO-892 when ready for allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures to assist in providing copies/access to references
rubrics_metrics.description: To assist in providing copies of, or access to, references, the examiner should: (A) Type the citation of the references on form PTO-892 ... (B) Include, in the action folder all of the references cited by the examiner which are to be furnished to the applicant. (C) After any necessary review has taken place, forward the action to the TC mailbox for counting. Any application which is submitted without all of the required references will be returned to the examiner. The missing reference(s) should be obtained and the file returned to the technical support staff as quickly as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow PTO-892 procedures, include copies in action folder, forward for counting; missing references cause returns and must be quickly corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: How applicants can obtain copies of cited U.S. patents and publications
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO does not provide copies of U.S. patents or U.S. patent application publications with Office actions. To obtain the below cited U.S. patent(s) or U.S. patent application publication(s), any of the following options may be used, free of charge: Patent Center; Patent Public Search tool; Patent and Trademark Resource Center (PTRC); commercial sources; or purchase certified copies from the Copy Fulfillment Branch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides step-by-step instructions and formatting rules (leading zeros, prefixes for design/reissue/plant patents) for using Patent Center and Patent Public Search, and contact info for certified copies and assistance centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of related art and information by applicants does not relieve examiner duty
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted citations will not in any way diminish the obligation of examiners to conduct independent prior art searches, or relieve examiners of citing other pertinent prior art of which they may be aware. Prior art submitted by applicant ... will not be supplied with an Office action. Any requirement to submit information under 37 CFR 1.105 ... will not in any way diminish the obligation of examiners to conduct independent prior art searches ... Information submitted by applicant in the manner provided ... will not be supplied with an Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant submissions (IDS or required information) do not substitute for examiner searches and are not necessarily furnished with Office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of listing references on PTO-892 and brief discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: In citing references for the first time, the identifying data of the citation should be placed on form PTO-892, 'Notice of References Cited,' a copy of which will be attached to the Office action. No distinction is to be made between references on which a claim is rejected and those formerly referred to as 'pertinent.' With the exception of applicant submitted citations ... it is the pertinent features of recommended references which are not used as a basis for rejection be pointed out briefly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PTO-892 for first-time citations; do not segregate 'rejection' vs 'pertinent' references; briefly point out pertinent features of recommended references not used as the basis for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: When applicant later refers to a reference relied upon by examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant in an amendatory paper refers to a reference that is subsequently relied upon by the examiner, such reference shall be cited by the examiner in the usual manner using a form PTO-892, 'Notice of References Cited,' unless applicant has listed the reference on a form PTO/SB/08 that has been initialed by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant brings a reference to the examiner's attention and the examiner later relies on it, cite it on PTO-892 unless PTO/SB/08 was used and initialed.
